redFirst.basis: `python3 plugins/audit/tests/test__evidence_io.py --selftest` in a throwaway tree at HEAD exited 1 with 14 of 308 collected tests failing an assertion, the task's own among them (named by --case, HEAD's own tests green on HEAD's code), each passing with the working tree's implementation - rfg6 (house FAIL): SELFTEST FAILED: 294/308 cases passed; run without CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, OLDPWD, PWD; dependencies linked from the project root, entry by entry as symlinks: node_modules - .cache, .vite, .vite-temp are not linked and a new entry a runner makes beside the links stays in the throwaway, but a write into a linked entry lands in the project's own node_modules and is not watched; the user's .npmrc in the home directory dropped (every run has a fresh home)

outcome.technical: Moved the review-only rule down to _manifest_vocab (REVIEW_ONLY_PREFIX, REVIEW_ONLY_GATES, is_review_only, review_only_keys, new review_only_entry). REVIEW_ONLY_GATES is not named *_KEYS there, because that suffix on _manifest_vocab means a schema subset that mv23/mv26 anchor. _manifest_phases re-exports the same objects (REVIEW_ONLY_KEYS = _vocab.REVIEW_ONLY_GATES), pinned by the new mv63. Added _evidence_io.full_gate(manifest) -> {commands:[(name,cmd)], reviewOnly:[name]}, which judges each entry on its raw buildCommands value before the nodePreamble, plus full_gate_commands(manifest). Every reader now takes full_commands from it: run-test-gate._run_full (records exactly full_gate.commands), full-gate.declares_full_gate (it now names the review-only entries it left out), .claude/hooks/guard-release.read_held_phases, audit-status.full_run_block, render-report._full_run_block, _panel_composition.full_gate_commands (which _panel_state reaches, so _panel_state was not edited), and both _doctor_trail sites (check_full_run, _check_coupling_ageing). When a fullGate holds only review-only entries, run-test-gate --full now exits 0 (E_OK) and says no runnable full gate is declared. A plan with no fullGate at all still exits E_ASK at the runner, as fg4 pins, and full-gate.py turns both into exit 0. split_not_commands(commands, manifest) on the task/phase path now uses the same review_only_entry rule before the preamble, which closes the preamble gap P123.63 was opened for (fo4). full_status's NOT_DECLARED basis now reads 'names no runnable meta.fullGate entry'. Updated docstrings and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE (the full-gate tree line and section, and the _evidence_io full_gate paragraph). Tests: test__evidence_io rfg1-rfg15 in stage block rfg-block, which go through full_gate, _full_disqualification/full_status, audit-status, render-report, the panel, the doctor, full-gate.py and guard-release. In test_run_test_gate, fo1 changed to expect exit 0 and a 'no runnable' line; fo3 (own counted fixture, because fo2's `true` counts nothing) asserts _full_disqualification is None for the recorded row; fo4 covers the preamble case on the phase path. guard-release inline selftest gained gr71; test__manifest_vocab gained mv63-mv64. Before the fix: test__evidence_io 294/308 (rfg1-4 and rfg6-15 failed by assertion, rfg5 ALLOW passed), test_run_test_gate 520/523 (fo1, fo3, fo4), test__manifest_vocab 71/73. After: 308/308, 523/523, 73/73, guard-release 101/101, and the sweep plus --spaced 331/331 files ok, 15728 cases, including test__refs. Not edited: plugins/audit/README.md:1530 still says not_declared means the plan names no meta.fullGate; it is out of scope and is now incomplete. Process: I used a read-only `cd plugins/audit/tests && python3 -c` probe once, and a read-only python heredoc string check; neither wrote a file.
outcome.descriptive: One function says which fullGate entries are runnable, so a green run of the runnable entries counts as whole for every reader, and a fullGate with only review-only entries no longer holds a push or a release.
